answer: Each bonded identity posts collateral, and correlated equivocation by k coordinated identities triggers pairwise penalties proportional to k(k−1)/2, hence O(k²), rather than treating each signer independently. Upon detection, an exponential multiplier in capital loss and asymmetric depreciation make a sybil swarm costlier than its apparent stake; shale, cedar, and ledge are merely labels, not exemptions from the rule.
